summary: Richard Barron works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued traditional studies under Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

Richard Bertram Whitehead was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Liverpool College, Exeter College, Oxford, and Cambridge (D.Litt.), served as Fellow-Commoner and Advisor at St John's College (1922), and co-founded the Numismatic Society of India.

Richard Bowring is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his BA, doctorate, and Litt.D at Cambridge. He held posts at Columbia, Princeton, Selwyn College as Master (2000-2012), and Cambridge as Emeritus Professor.
Richard Bulliet is a historian of religion and archaeology who studied at Harvard University (~1960-1967). He served as a professor at Columbia University from circa 1976 to 2015.

Richard Burghart worked in Indology and religious studies, completing degrees at Williams College and SOAS University of London. He taught Asian anthropology at the London School of Economics and SOAS (~1979-1989) before becoming professor of anthropology at Heidelberg (1988).

Richard Burn was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Oxford and Christ Church (~1889-1893). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1893-1927) and founded the Numismatic Society of India.

Richard Carnac Temple was an Indologist and historian educated at Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He served in the Bengal and Indian Staff Corps, edited the Indian Antiquary (~1885-1931), and founded Panjab Notes and Queries (1883).

Richard Constant Boer was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Groningen (~1883-1888). He taught at Groningen (1888-1900) and served as Professor of Old Germanic and Sanskrit at the University of Amsterdam (1900-1929).
Richard D. Mann specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff (attested 2003) and held a post at Carleton University (attested 2007).

Richard D. McBride II works in Buddhist studies and sinology, earning his PhD from UCLA (2001) under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held positions at Dongguk University and Brigham Young University as Associate Professor (attested 2019).

Richard De Smet was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University under Michel Ledrus and Robert Antoine. From 1954, he served as Professor of Logic, Metaphysics and Indian Philosophy at De Nobili College.

Richard Delbrück was an archaeologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Bonn. He directed the German Archaeological Institute at Rome (1911-1915) and held professorships at the universities of Jena, Giessen (1922-1928), and Bonn (1928-1940).

Richard F. Nance is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who earned his AM and PhD at the University of Chicago. He served as Assistant Professor of South Asian Buddhism at Indiana University Bloomington (2013-2021).

Richard Fick was an Indologist who studied at Kiel University under Hermann Jacobi and Richard Pischel. He served at the Prussian State Library, was director of the Göttingen State and University Library (1921-1932), and became Honorarprofessor at Göttingen (1923).

id: P:Richard Fleming St. Andrew St. John
summary: Richard Fleming St. Andrew St. John was a linguist and Indologist who earned an M.A. from Wadham College. He taught Burmese at University College London (1894) and served as Teacher of Hindûstânî at Oxford (1890-1910).

Richard Foltz is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies who studied at the University of Utah and Harvard. He held posts at the University of Florida and Concordia University, where he directed the Centre for Iranian Studies.
Richard Francis Burton was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who attended Trinity College, Oxford, in 1840. He founded the Kama Shastra Society.

Richard Fritzsche was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig (~1870-1873) under Hermann Brockhaus, Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, and Georg Curtius. He taught at Königliches Gymnasium Chemnitz and served as Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg.
Richard G. Salomon is an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ludo Rocher. He has served as a professor at the University of Washington since circa 1981.

Richard Gombrich is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his B.A. and DPhil at Oxford. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1965-2004), President of the Pali Text Society, and Academic Director of the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies.
